output.deciding_quote: allows for sensitive information disclosure when configured as a Gateway (VPN virtual server, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or AAA virtual server.
output.case_for_each_candidate: Case for affected (Candidate 1): the inventory names the product as NetScaler ADC and gives no edition marker. The matching NVD row is the standard-edition ('-') CPE netscaler_application_delivery_controller with versionStartIncluding=13.1 and versionEndExcluding=13.1-49.15. Build 13.1-49.13 is at or above 13.1 and below 13.1-49.15, so the installed version falls inside an affected range. The definition of affected is met on version alone. The 13.1 FIPS row (ending at 13.1-37.164) and the 12.1-only ndcpp row do not contain this build, but nothing in the inventory says the unit is FIPS or NDcPP. Case for conditional (Candidate 2): the version is affected, as above. Both KEV and the NVD description, however, limit the vulnerability to an appliance "configured as a Gateway (VPN virtual server, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or AAA virtual server". That is a configuration condition. The inventory records only vendor, product, version and hostname, so it cannot say whether a Gateway or AAA vserver exists. That is exactly the situation the spec defines as conditional: the version is affected, but exposure depends on configuration the inventory does not record. Decision: conditional. The version check settles the first half of the definition, and the documents' explicit Gateway/AAA precondition, which the inventory cannot resolve, settles the second.
output.disagreements: Candidate 1 (affected) stops at the version check. Both documents state an explicit configuration precondition (Gateway or AAA virtual server), and the inventory does not record it. Under the given definitions, a version-affected item whose exposure depends on unrecorded configuration is conditional, not affected. Candidate 1 gave no reasoning, so the error is one of omission: it applies the definition of affected without testing the narrower conditional definition that the documents trigger. Candidate 2, second rationale: "the unrecorded edition matters too" overstates the edition point. Edition is not a feature or configuration in the sense of the conditional definition. If edition really were in doubt, it would push the label toward unknown or not_affected (the 13.1 FIPS row ends at 13.1-37.164, so a FIPS unit at 49.13 would fall outside it), not toward conditional. So edition cannot be a supporting reason for conditional. The recorded product is plain "NetScaler ADC" with no FIPS or NDcPP marker, and the standard-edition row is the natural match. Candidate 2, first and third rationales: they list "edition is not recorded either" as an additional factor alongside the configuration condition. That is the same mistake in a milder form. It is a non-sequitur for this label: the label rests only on the Gateway/AAA configuration condition, and adding edition implies a second conditional factor that the definition does not recognize. The core reasoning of all three Candidate 2 rationales (49.13 < 49.15 on the '-' row, plus the unrecorded Gateway/AAA configuration) is correct. Minor point for completeness: the NVD config also lists separate netscaler_gateway CPE rows. The inventory product is NetScaler ADC, so the ADC rows are the ones that govern. None of the candidates misapplied this, but none stated it.
output.real_world_note: Outside knowledge would not change the real-world answer away from conditional. It would remove the edition doubt that Candidate 2 raises. Citrix bulletin CTX579459 (linked from the KEV notes) lists 13.1-49.15 as the fixed standard 13.1 build. FIPS builds are numbered on a separate 13.1-37.x line, so a build numbered 13.1-49.13 is a standard-edition release, and the FIPS question does not arise in practice. The vendor also confirms that only appliances configured as Gateway or AAA vservers are vulnerable (this is the "Citrix Bleed" session-token leak). An operator would check for those vservers. If any exist, the operator would treat the unit as exploitable and, besides upgrading, kill active and persistent sessions, as the KEV requiredAction says. None of this changes the dataset label, which rests on the documents and definitions alone.
